messages:
incident-bot: P1 Alert — Canary group 'gen-3' reports 5xx spike and progressive OOMs during traffic shift. Auto-escalation to oncall.

deploy-bot: Deploy job 2026-03-15T11:22Z started: rollout/gen-3 -> 10% traffic

sara: seeing elevated 500s on canary-3-2, logs show repeated OOM: \"out of memory trying to allocate KV cache\". Keeping watch.

mike: can confirm. CPU ok but memory creeping up per pod. Snapshot: gen-3-2 mem RSS 28G -> 31G in 5m. We shifted from 0% -> 10% ~2m ago.

eli: tagging @oncall-bob — paging now. Can you take lead? I can try a conservative traffic rollback.

oncall-bob: on it. Pulling up dashboards (dash.redwood.internal/canary/gen-3). Prioritize customer-facing rollback if impacts >1% of requests.

ops-tilly: quick note — only Dedicated clusters in us-east-1 were part of this canary (non-hosted). CS flagged a slow request from a large customer earlier.

jane: status from deploy-bot? Can we pause/abort the rollout? Need to prevent more canaries hitting OOM.

deploy-bot: Action queued: rollback rollout/gen-3 to previous stable (gen-2) at 2026-03-15T11:28Z. Executing traffic shift to 0% canary.

sara: sending small logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T11:24:12Z gen-3-2 kernel: oom-killer invoked: process llm_infer(pid=21452)
2026-03-15T11:24:12Z gen-3-2 llm_infer: kv_cache_alloc failed: requested 2.4G
2026-03-15T11:24:13Z gen-3-2 proxy: returning 503 to client
```

mike: applied network-level traffic shift to 0% for canary group. Confirming pods draining.

eli: I see pods terminating, but one pod restarted and immediately hit OOM on restart. Possible memory leak triggered by certain sequence lengths / prompt shapes.

oncall-bob: Good. Starting mitigation checklist: 1) rollback (in progress), 2) kill-switch feature-flag to prevent canary auto-apply, 3) notify CS and affected customers, 4) collect heap/profile from crashed pods.

pm-lucia: tagging product — is this rollout tied to a new memory larger KV-cache default? We changed default cache prefetch in 2.1.0.

jane: yes, gen-3 includes kv-cache prefetch on by default for throughput. We should flip feature flag off for Dedicated until we have better guardrails.

ops-tilly: CS reports 1 major Dedicated customer saw ~0.8% increased 5xx rate during the window. Not widespread but high priority for that customer.

cs-amy: notified the customer and offered workaround: route that team's traffic to stable region. They're asking for ETA on fix and rollback confirmation.

oncall-bob: rollback completed at 1843500187. Canary traffic back to 0%. Let's validate overall 5xx rate normalizing.

mike: metrics: global 5xx spike down from 1.9% -> 0.12% over the last 3m. Dedicated us-east returning to baseline.

eli: capturing diagnostic artifacts: heap profile, /proc/meminfo, and container logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1843500012/canary-gen3/ — link: https://s3.redwood/internal/1843500012

sara: started gcore and heapdump on one restarted pod before it was evicted, file names: heapdump_21452.hprof

oncall-bob: handing off to afternoon oncall @eli for continued investigation and postmortem. I'm rotating out in 20m. Please own customer comms and RCA.

eli: taking handoff. I'll open an incident ticket (INC-18435) and schedule a quick blameless postmortem. Also will create a temporary feature-flag revert (ff/kv-prefetch) for Dedicated deployments.

pm-lucia: can you also add a rollout policy change: disable automatic canary for Dedicated until mem regression tests added? We should prevent auto-traffic shifts >5% without SLO checks.

jane: agreed. I'll create a gating PR for the rollout controller and add an integration test that simulates large KV sizes.

cs-amy: customer replied: thanks for quick rollback, they'll monitor and want a follow-up email. Please ping me with the RCA summary once available.

incident-bot: Incident updated: INC-18435 assigned to eli, severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 after rollback and no ongoing errors at 11:30Z.

eli: noted. Immediate action items: 1) collect full heap/profile review (in progress), 2) revert feature flag for Dedicated (done at 11:41Z), 3) add canary gating to rollout controller (ticket PR queued), 4) draft customer follow-up.

oncall-bob: thanks team. I'll leave notes in runbook: may need to add OOM guard in the autoscaler for inference pods (limit request/reserve heuristics).

sara: quick follow — logs show certain prompts cause kv_cache_alloc requests > configured cap. We should add sanity cap at runtime to fail gracefully instead of OOMing.

eli: putting that on the action list. Postmortem owners: eli (lead), jane (dev), mike (metrics), cs-amy (customer comms). ETA for preliminary RCA: 1 business day.

pm-lucia: good. Please include timeline, affected customers, rollback decision rationale, and follow-up mitigations in the RCA.

cs-amy: sending template to eli for customer-facing summary.

mike: leaving one final note — let's add a small canary test that feeds long-context prompts to new gen models during staging.

oncall-bob: closing my shift — all handoffs complete. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:

eli: thanks, taking over. Will post updates to INC-18435 thread and create follow-up issue TKT-18435-rca.

incident-bot: Thread archived (auto) — incident state: monitoring.
